uncited: Volumetric and Atmospheric Rendering is a family of techniques that render participating media (clouds, fog, smoke) and planetary atmospheres by integrating light transport along rays.

It differs from [SDF Cloud Rendering](2064-sdf-cloud-rendering.md) by solving the radiative transfer equation (or approximations like single scattering) rather than constructing explicit geometry via Signed Distance Fields, and from [Ray Marching with Single Scattering](2057-ray-marching-with-single-scattering.md) by focusing on global atmospheric phenomena rather than localized procedural clouds.
Unlike surface rendering, the ray accumulates color and opacity as it traverses the medium.
The position is advanced: $p \leftarrow p + \Delta s \cdot v$ [S10].
The technique originated in real-time graphics for rendering clouds and fog.
